title: Keep VAT off electricity after July 2027
name: Keep VAT off electricity after July 2027
headline: Keep the zero rate after July 2027. Costs about £1.4bn a year.
description: The Budget takes VAT off domestic electricity in Great Britain from 1 October 2026 to 1 July 2027, scored at £755m for the half year to March and £305m for the quarter to June. This card keeps the rate at 0% after July 2027: a full year is the Treasury’s half year plus two of its quarters, held flat in cash, for the part of each year the Budget’s zero rate does not already cover.

baselinePolicy.text: Domestic fuel and power pay the 5% reduced rate, except electricity, at 0% from 1 October 2026 to 1 July 2027 (Table 6.1 line 2).

source.quote: This measure is effective from 1 October 2026 until 1 July 2027.

alreadyIncludes: The zero rate on domestic electricity from 1 October 2026 to 1 July 2027 (Budget 2026, Table 6.1 line 2).

terms.label: Cost of a full year of the zero rate: the Treasury’s half year to March 2027 plus two of its quarters to June 2027, negative because receipts fall

source.note: line 2: 755 in 2026-27 (October to March) and 305 in 2027-28 (April to June); July to September is taken as the April to June quarter again

terms.label: Share of each year the Budget’s zero rate does not already cover

source.note: The zero rate runs to 1 July 2027, so the first quarter of 2027-28 is already in the forecast.

rawSource.note: The Treasury’s own certified figures for the zero rate, held flat in cash: a full year is its half year plus two of its quarters, and the first quarter of 2027-28 is already in the baseline.

caveats: The July to September quarter is taken as the April to June quarter again, which is our assumption; summer use is lower than winter, so a full year costs less than twice the winter half.
Held flat in cash: a growing VAT base would cost more, and nothing published says how much.
Great Britain only, as the zero rate is; Northern Ireland stays at 5% under the Windsor Framework arrangements HMRC describes.
Static: no change in electricity use is allowed for.

considerations.text: Cheaper electricity means a little more of it is used, and the shift from gas to heat pumps and electric cars raises the base the relief sits on year by year; the card grows with VAT receipts overall, not with electricity demand.

The government put the saving at about £45 a year on a price-cap bill. It is a flat share of every bill, so it is worth more in cash to bigger users and more as a share of income to poorer households.

interactions.text: The gas card’s arithmetic treats electricity as zero-rated for good. Without this card, electricity returns to 5% in April 2027 while gas stays at 0%.
The reduced-rate slider moves the 5% rate on all domestic fuel and power; with electricity at 0% it reaches gas and other fuels only, so the two together overstate.
